Subject: ACME bench results (retail prompt set)

Hi Alex / Samira / Marissa — thanks for the ping. Attached are the benchmark artifacts and a short summary below. Test harness details are included in the CSV.

Test config (summary):
- Model: redwood-13b (4-bit quantized)
- Sequence length: prompt ~40 tokens, generation target 128 tokens
- Hardware: Dedicated NVIDIA H100 (single-GPU runs), baseline kernel selection
- Harness: 1,000 prompts drawn from ACME sample set, measured end-to-end (tokenize -> generate -> detokenize)
- Concurrency tests: single-request (batch=1), and simulated 500 concurrent sessions using our autoscale emulator with steady-state arrival rate

Summary numbers (end-to-end):
- Single-request (batch=1): p50 = 95 ms, p95 = 230 ms
- Batching @ batch_size=8 (packed requests): effective latency per request p50 = 120 ms, p95 = 320 ms (note: batching increases throughput but widens tail for individual requests)
- Simulated 500 concurrent sessions with dedicated pool + autoscaling: 99th percentile observed ~480 ms in our steady-state run (transient spikes during scaling events up to ~700 ms)
- Throughput: sustained token throughput on the dedicated pool observed 4,200 tokens/sec for the workload when batching at 8 across the pool

Notes / mitigation:
- We recommend using prefix caching for stable prompts (reduces p95 by ~30% for reuse-heavy flows).
- For hard SLOs at p95 < 250 ms we typically advise: dedicated pool with reserved headroom + conservative autoscale policy + smaller batch sizes (1–4).

Attachments: acme_benchmarks_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB) — contains graphs and per-run distributions; acme_perf_summary.csv (CSV, 12KB) — raw run-level metrics.

If useful I can run a tuned pass (smaller batch sizes + cache enabled) against your exact prompt set and return a targeted config with expected p95. Happy to schedule a short run.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
